newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine foreign loans approvals up 29 pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: Philippine foreign loans approvals up 29 pct in 96.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Thursday it had approved $8.048 billion worth of medium to long term foreign loans last year, up 29 percent from $6.234 billion approved in the previous year.

Private sector loans rose by 3.0 percent to $3.412 billion from $3.316 billion, while loans contracted by the public sector reached $4.636 billion or 59 percent higher than the previous year's $2.917 billion, the Central Bank's Management of External Debt Department chief Cristina Orbeta said.

Most of the loans contracted by the government and state-owned firms went to energy and power projects, totalling $1.315 billion. The other public sector loans were used for refinancing, $948 million, and to finance infrastructure projects, $704 million.

In private sector borrowings, multilateral and bilateral sources topped the list of creditors with a combined commitment of $2.925 billion, while bond buyers ranked second purchasing $1.572 billion worth of bonds and notes.

The figures excluded the Floating Rate Certificates of Deposits issued by banks which amounted to $1.32 billion; loans with grant element of at least 35 percent, $1.485 billion; and the $551 million bonds issued under the Philippine Brady Exchange Programme. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
